content:
Here's the analysis.

---

## What "no priority" means today

We have seven items. Four have an empty `triaged_by` **and** an empty `marked` (priority). Three have both a triager and a priority set.

| Task | Created | triaged_by | marked | Status |
|------|---------|-----------|--------|--------|
| T-0911 | Jan 28 08:14 | — | — | untouched |
| T-0912 | Jan 28 09:02 | r-okafor | high | triaged |
| T-0913 | Jan 28 09:40 | — | — | untouched |
| T-0914 | Jan 29 11:15 | r-okafor | normal | triaged |
| T-0915 | Jan 29 13:47 | — | — | untouched |
| T-0916 | Jan 30 07:05 | s-lindqvist | high | triaged |
| T-0917 | Jan 30 10:22 | — | — | untouched |

The CSV is sorted by `created_at` ascending, so the newest items are at the bottom. But the triage policy describes a different **working order**:

> *"Four of the seven items … have never been read by anyone. They are the four at the bottom of the list."*

The "*bottom of the list*" here isn't creation order — it's the **working order** the triager walks. The untouched items (T-0911, T-0913, T-0915, T-0917) are pulled to the end of the queue even though T-0911 is the oldest. **An empty priority is currently a signal for "unread / never seen by a human."** It doesn't mean "no opinion yet" — it means the item hasn't even been evaluated.

### The implicit queue-ordering today

Walking the policy's logic, the queue is effectively sorted as:

1. **High** — triaged and explicitly bumped up (T-0912, T-0916)
2. **Normal** — triaged and kept in place (T-0914)
3. *(everything below here: untouched)*
4. **Unread** (empty priority) — oldest-first among themselves (T-0911 → T-0913 → T-0915 → T-0917)

Critically, **a triaged "normal" item sits above every unread item**, even if the unread item is much older. The triage policy says this explicitly: *"An item nobody has read yet is worked last, after everything a human has already looked at and kept."*

---

## Recommended default

**A record arriving without a priority should default to a sentinel value representing `"untriaged"` (not set, empty, or `null`), and the queue ordering must place this below any explicit priority assigned by a human.**

Do **not** default to `"low"` or `"normal"`. Here's why:

| If default is… | Then… |
|---|---|
| `null` / empty | Stays at the bottom, matching current behavior. Once triaged, a human sets an explicit value and the item moves up relative to untouched items. |
| `"low"` | An unread item would be considered "already triaged as low priority" — but nobody has read it. Also, the team may later want a real "low" to mean "read and judged unimportant," which should still rank above truly unread work. |
| `"normal"` | New items would immediately interleave with triaged normal items, violating the policy that unread items are worked last. |

Use `null` (or a specific value like `"untriaged"` or `"unread"`) so the sort logic becomes:

```text
high > normal > low > untriaged(null)
```

This preserves the existing behavior exactly: an item lands at the bottom of the working queue, stays there until a human reads it, and only then rises above other untouched items (or jumps further if marked `high`). The four unread items in the backlog would continue to be worked after the three that `r-okafor` and `s-lindqvist` have already touched.

Right, that is how the queue works. Decision: priority is optional and an unset priority means nobody has triaged the record yet, so it defaults to the floor of the scale. An untriaged item must never outrank something a human has already looked at and marked, and defaulting anywhere above the bottom would do exactly that.
